office_does: A Spokane County District Court judge, elected countywide for four years, hears misdemeanor and gross-misdemeanor criminal cases, traffic and civil cases, small claims and protection orders; the main discretion is in release, sentencing, probation and therapeutic-court supervision.
race_blurb: Open seat: Judge Jeffrey Smith is retiring and endorses Spokane Municipal Court Commissioner Mike Valerien, a former city prosecutor. Valerien faces attorney and pro tem judge Deanna Crull, whose practice mixes prosecution and public defense and who narrowly lost a 2022 District Court race. Both carry an 'Exceptionally Well Qualified' bar rating, and many local judges endorse both.

candidates.summary: Spokane Municipal Court commissioner since 2016 after eight years as a City of Spokane assistant prosecutor; Air Force veteran and former 911 operator. Says judges should apply the law as the Legislature wrote it.
highlights: Full-time Spokane Municipal Court commissioner since 2016, including therapeutic-court hearings [S3][S4]
Eight years as a city prosecutor, including Veteran's Court [S4][S7]
"The Legislature passes the laws and it's my job to enforce the law as they've written it" [S7]
Rated Exceptionally Well Qualified by the Spokane County Bar Association panel (2026) [S6]
Endorsed by retiring incumbent Jeff Smith, Prosecutor Preston McCollam and the Spokane Police Guild [S5][S7]

judicial.basis: States an apply-the-law-as-written philosophy (Legislature writes, judge enforces as written, subject to the Constitution), with discretion reserved for sentencing and probation.

safety.basis: Prosecution formation and an 'hold offenders accountable' pledge, balanced by therapeutic-court work and his statement that 'we are not able to prosecute ourselves from these problems'; no bail position.

experience.basis: Not an incumbent, but runs on ten years of full-time bench service as a commissioner and is endorsed by the retiring incumbent.

candidates.summary: Attorney and law-firm owner since 2009 who has served as a District Court pro tem judge since 2019, Airway Heights court commissioner since 2020 and a judge on several tribal courts; her practice has included prosecution and contract public defense.
highlights: District Court pro tem judge since 2019 and Airway Heights Municipal Court commissioner since 2020 [S1][S2]
Former city and county prosecutor; contract public defender in Lincoln and Adams counties [S2]
Backs therapeutic alternatives for "qualified, motivated individuals" while stressing accountability [S1][S6]
Used her 2022 SCBA rating (Exceptionally Well Qualified); skipped the 2026 evaluation and bar poll [S5]
Lost the 2022 District Court Position 6 race, 48.6% to 50.7% [S8]

judicial.basis: Describes a problem-solving, individualized approach that weighs history, circumstances and rehabilitation; says 'the old ways no longer serve the community' and stresses access to justice.

safety.basis: Mixed formation with long-running public-defense work, plus support for therapeutic alternatives and early intervention, qualified by an emphasis on accountability and community safety; no bail position.

experience.basis: Not an incumbent, but runs on 25 years of practice and seven years of pro tem, commissioner and tribal-court judicial service.
